subject.title: Workspace symlinks to ~/.openclaw subdirectories are rejected by boundary path check

question: Should fixed workspace bootstrap files be allowed to follow symlink targets outside the workspace root when the target is under the OpenClaw home tree, and what roots must stay blocked?
rationale: The failure is source-reproducible, but the fix decides which external local files can become automatic startup prompt context and a member explicitly asked for active fs-safe/OpenClaw wrapper policy plus security tests.

options.title: Land a scoped bootstrap-only exception
options.body: Allow only fixed bootstrap-file symlink hops to approved regular-file targets while rejecting direct arbitrary `.openclaw` paths and private state roots.

options.title: Keep strict boundary with diagnostics
options.body: Continue rejecting external symlink targets but render boundary-blocked bootstrap files distinctly from missing files so users can diagnose the setup.

options.title: Require explicit trusted paths
options.body: Add a configured allowlist before loading external symlink targets, accepting a new config surface and upgrade documentation burden.

recommendation.title: Land a scoped bootstrap-only exception
recommendation.body: Allow only fixed bootstrap-file symlink hops to approved regular-file targets while rejecting direct arbitrary `.openclaw` paths and private state roots.

likelyOwner.reason: He owns the active maintainer-labeled replacement PR and posted the current maintainer direction on this issue.
